claims.text: CALPHAD-based thermodynamic modeling can accurately predict melting temperatures across a wide compositional range of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based thermodynamic modeling can accurately predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion across a wide compositional range of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based thermodynamic modeling can accurately predict volume changes at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a wide compositional range of high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD provides an efficient method for determining these fusion and liquid-phase properties.
The proposed modeling uses established phase-equilibrium and fusion-property databases calibrated against experimental data.
Database parameters can be updated using information from binary and ternary subsystems.
Phase equilibria and energetic interactions among alloying elements govern melting behavior and fusion thermodynamics.
Energy minimization and phase-stability calculations permit estimation of melting and fusion properties.
The CALPHAD framework accounts for multicomponent energetic interactions and liquid-phase behavior.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change will lie within an acceptable error margin relative to experiments.
Predicted liquid-phase properties will agree well with measured thermodynamic data.
Existing experimental measurements and empirical models often have limited generalizability and efficiency for high-entropy alloys.
The approach should be reliable when the relevant binary and ternary subsystems are well characterized.
Significant short-range order, magnetic effects, or unanticipated complex interactions can reduce prediction accuracy.
Quantitative accuracy may deteriorate in poorly characterized compositional regions.
Errors greater than an approximately 10% threshold across multiple key properties in a statistically significant alloy set would falsify the proposed accuracy claim.
